topics.label: Introduction to the Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of Innate Immune Recognition via PAMPs and DAMPs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how the innate immune system recognizes signs of infection and tissue damage through conserved molecular patterns and germline-encoded receptors.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptor Families and Inflammasome Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the specific receptor classes, intracellular signaling pathways, and multi-protein inflammasome complexes that detect pathogens and stress.

topics.label: Cellular Activation, Leukocyte Recruitment, and Systemic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how sentinel cells respond to infection by releasing mediators, recruiting immune cells into tissues, draining antigens to lymph nodes, and potentially triggering severe systemic reactions.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammatory Responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the active and passive mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation, how damaged tissue is repaired, and how the host responds to persistent inflammatory stimuli.

topics.label: Conclusion and Next Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming topic on the complement system.
